title: Sigma0 26.5 oxygen loss began near 1990 at 160 E-180, where the winter outcrop shrank; oxygen there follows outcrop area at a 1-yr lag; 4 of 7 CMIP6 models do not ventilate 26.5 (1950-2025)
abstract: Question: where does the within-water-type oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 that reaches California (CalCOFI) start, and why do climate models not make it? Approach: we extended World Ocean Database ship analyses of this surface west to 140 E (1950-2025), measured the winter outcrop of the 26.5 class in 30-50 N, 140 E-150 W with raw ship casts against WOA23 and with EN4.2.2, tested lagged links in time and out of sample (fit 1950-2006, test 2007-2025), and calculated the same outcrop indices in seven CMIP6 runs. Results: winter surface sigma0 in the outcrop region fell by 0.15 kg/m3 from 1984-1996 to 2009-2025 (ship casts), and the EN4 area with sigma0 >= 26.5 fell by 73%. Within-type oxygen fell by 13-18 umol/kg in all western regions. The decline started first at 36-46 N, 170-180 E (ramp midpoint 1989) and 160-170 E (1991.5), where the 26.4-26.6 layer thinned by 20-30 m, and moved east at about 2 cm/s to CalCOFI (2000). Near Japan (145-160 E) it came only in 2010-2014. At 160 E-180, within-type oxygen followed the EN4 outcrop area with a 1-year lag (detrended r 0.45-0.55, surrogate p 0.003-0.027), in the ship era and the Argo era. Downstream the lag was 5-6 years. A lag model with outcrop area forecast about half of the 2007-2025 CalCOFI low (-7.1 vs -14.6 umol/kg) and did not beat persistence. In 4 of 7 CMIP6 models the 26.5 surface does not outcrop in the region (winter surface density 0.23-0.51 kg/m3 too low); in the other 3 the outcrop area fell by only 20-36% (EN4: 73%). Interpretation: the loss started where the class is subducted in the central North Pacific, as its outcrop shrank, and models miss it partly because most do not ventilate this density there. Limitations: the year-to-year link depends on the EN4 analysis (not redistributed; NCGL terms); the public ship index confirms only the epoch change; surface density is a proxy for subduction; many tests; one member per model.
